instructions: You are one of two independent readers for a public record that scores theories of consciousness. A study counts toward a prediction only if that prediction was on record, in a dated publication by the theory's own proponents, before the study first appeared. A study that says it set out to test a theory tests nothing if the prediction was first written in the same paper (or the study's own registration). When the dates or the commitment are unclear, the study is not counted. Read the passages and dates. Decide: BEFORE (the earlier passage commits the theory to this prediction, and it predates the study), NOT-BEFORE (it does not), or UNCLEAR. Answer in JSON: {"verdict": "before"|"not-before"|"unclear", "reason": "two to four plain sentences", "unsure": true|false, "unsure_why": "..."}.

core_claim.quote: Ignition is characterized by the sudden, coherent, and exclusive activation of a subset of workspace neurons coding for the current conscious content, with the remainder of the workspace neurons being inhibited.

source.citation: Mashour GA, Roelfsema P, Changeux J-P, Dehaene S. Conscious processing and the global neuronal workspace hypothesis. Neuron 105(5):776-798, 2020

prediction.statement: When a lasting conscious stimulus disappears, a second brief ignition occurs in prefrontal cortex, updating the workspace.

first_stated.passage: A brief ignition is also expected at the offset of the stimuli, reflecting the conscious update at the moment of the disappearance of the stimulus.

source.citation: Melloni L, Mudrik L, Pitts M, et al. Preregistration file v1, January 2019: Accelerating research on consciousness: an adversarial collaboration to test contradictory predictions of global neuronal workspace and integrated information theory. OSF project mbcfy, component wz8mj

prediction.test_for: A transient prefrontal response about 0.3 to 0.5 s after the offset of a consciously seen stimulus, as well as at its onset.
prediction.test_against: Prefrontal responses at onset but none at offset, in a design that finds offset responses elsewhere.

study.name: The Cogitate Consortium's adversarial test of global workspace and integrated information theory

source.citation: Cogitate Consortium, Ferrante O, Gorska-Klimowska U, Henin S, et al. Adversarial testing of global neuronal workspace and integrated information theories of consciousness. Nature 642:133-142, 2025

passages.text: According to predictive theories, any discrepancy between sensory inputs and their internal models causes the production of a transient prediction error signal

source.citation: Melloni L, Mudrik L, Pitts M, Bendtz K, Ferrante O, ... Dehaene S, Koch C, Tononi G, Ward LM. An adversarial collaboration protocol for testing contrasting predictions of global neuronal workspace and integrated information theory. PLOS ONE 18(2):e0268577, 2023
